- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the low-end of the range to avoid underestimating downside risk.  
- Model tends to overestimate short-term volatility after recent spikes; apply a 3–5 day lag correction to smooth out immediate post-spike peaks.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–4% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, forecast should not exceed 1.5–2% above the 18-day moving average; otherwise, cap the forecast.  
- Overshoot after sentiment spikes: if sentiment rises sharply and forecast rises >15% from prior peak, subtract 5–8% from the forecast to avoid overcorrection.
